translation: The Ren is the sea of the yin vessels. Its vessel arises below Zhongji (CV3), within the lower abdomen, at the region of Huiyin (CV1). (Between the two genitals.) It ascends and emerges externally, runs along Qugu (CV2), (in the hollow of the pubic hair margin on the pubic bone) ascends the pubic hair margin, reaches Zhongji (CV3), (four cun below the navel, the u募u (front-mu) of the bladder) and together with Foot-Jueyin, Foot-Taiyin, and Foot-Shaoyin runs parallel within the abdomen, along Guanyuan (CV4), (three cun below the navel, the mu of the small intestine, the meeting of the three yin and the Ren vessel) passes Shimen (CV5) (that is, the Dantian, also called Mingmen, two cun below the navel, the mu of the Sanjiao) and Qihai (CV6), (one and a half cun below the navel in the hollow, the sea of engendering qi in men) and meets Foot-Shaoyang and the Chong vessel at Yinjiao (CV7). (One cun below the navel, at the upper opening of the bladder, the mu of the Sanjiao.) It runs along Shenque (CV8), (the center of the navel) and Shuifen (CV9), (one cun above the navel, at the lower opening of the small intestine) and meets Foot-Taiyin at Xiawan (CV10).
